Svencioneliai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vilniaus apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Svencioneliai developed around a new railway station on the St. Petersburg-Warsaw line, opened in 1861; as a major transport hub, frequent delays created strong demand for hotels and inns, a stable income source for many local Jewish families. For a long time the town had no cemetery of its own, and the deceased were taken to nearby Svencionys instead; only in 1911 did a local cemetery finally open. In September 1941, all of the town's Jews, along with several thousand more brought from nearby towns and villages, were relocated to barracks in a former Soviet military camp; beginning October 8, they were shot in small groups into a pre-dug pit over several days, men first and then women and children — an estimated 8,000 people were executed in total.
